---
title: Model candidates specification
---

`data_models` is a mutable model-selection card after preparation, with or without an upstream `obs_resample` plan.
It reads the JSON catalogue through `estimator_catalogue`. Explicit Commit constructs an unfitted recipe; browsing performs no fitting, installation or automatic model selection. Pure `_analyze`
and `_table` helpers separate requirements from display filters.

Requirements derive from the modeling context and `model_predictors`. Structural
requirements use assigned Sequence/Geometry and repeated Identifier roles. Forecasting
is an explicit exploration control because upstream outcome task and forecasting
objective are distinct. Unknown domain support never passes as compatible.

Default display includes compatible recipes regardless of package availability;
optional controls expose excluded/unreviewed recipes and hide uninstalled packages.
The table supports row selection and filtering. Details include parameters, conditions,
subjective assessments and evidence URLs. Missing evaluation plans remain browsable.
Unsupported types, infinities and empty datasets produce no compatible matches.

Settings persist through standard card configuration. Display-only settings
must not invalidate analysis. Exports return the incoming proxy independently of
settings and table rendering. No extended task or mutable-card commit is necessary.

Acceptance checks cover mixed/missing predictors, roles, survival requirements,
unsupported input, unresolved targets, structural uncertainty, installation filtering,
unchanged data, visible diagnostics and browser table/flip interactions. Catalogue
schema/version/probe checks remain in `tests/test_estimator_catalogue.py`.


The flip-side recipe is a single intrinsic-height, scrolling panel with separate
readiness/evidence badges and responsive section columns. It contains no Notes
output. Data-specific warnings remain on the front; general catalogue and
evaluation caveats are in the card documentation. Compact, narrow and full-screen
layouts must preserve readable headings and access to the final references.


Candidate rows group by estimator ID after per-recipe display filtering. Counts
identify the represented configurations; Type and Summary recipe are not displayed. Summary fields
come from one deterministically ranked recipe; capabilities and evidence are never
merged. Multi-recipe methods expose separate expandable detail panels.

Model taxonomy is stored in catalogue schema 1.4.0, with explicit source mappings
in `taxonomy.json` and static expansion in `model_taxonomy.py`. Five structured
attributes accompany the existing recipe `outputs` list and its `output_review`:
core mechanism, composition, fitting criterion, learning strategy and transparency.
Each classification has values, a review status and a qualification; shared sources
and review date are attached. Capacity growth must remain deferred for stage 2.
New unlisted methods are not classified from name substrings. Preparation-only
entries have a not-applicable predictive taxonomy. Recipe refinements are guarded
by exact configuration and reviewed package version; changed recipes revert to
method-level descriptions and unreviewed output support pending review.

The table exposes six descriptive columns with DataGrid sorting; column filters remain disabled. Its stable
hidden estimator index must survive filtering and sorting. Descriptions are compared
across the displayed recipes: differing labels produce `Varies by recipe`, never a
union of guarantees. The flip side shows the actual recipe descriptions, qualifications
and source links. These descriptions never change compatibility or selectability.
`class_prediction` is normalized to `class_label`; legacy output queries accept both.
Default hinge SGDClassifier and probability-disabled SVC recipes cannot satisfy a
class-probability requirement. Probabilities are not a calibration-quality guarantee.

`build_estimator_catalogue.py --refresh-descriptions` updates the saved snapshot
without importing or fitting estimators and without replacing prior probe evidence.
Normal rebuilds apply the same taxonomy registry. Focused checks cover schema,
refresh reproducibility, source output consistency, changed configuration guards,
component/hybrid distinctions, output support, grouped descriptions and UI selection.

Formulation is removed from the taxonomy and from both card faces. Prediction outputs
summarizes regression recipes as `Point prediction` or `Point prediction & spread`.
Spread requires explicit prediction-specific uncertainty outputs; no inference from
core mechanism, fitting criterion, coefficient errors or ensemble composition is allowed.
A lone quantile remains a point output, with its exact meaning shown in the details.
GaussianProcessRegressor, BayesianRidge and ARDRegression record return_std support;
GPR also records return_cov. The output requirement `prediction_spread` matches any
reviewed spread-output kind. Classification and specialist output distinctions remain.

Learning strategy uses reviewed `eager`, `lazy` or `hybrid` values and separate
configuration-dependent/unreviewed/not-applicable statuses. It describes the predictor,
not routine preprocessing, runtime, data retention or incremental updates. Explicit
method mappings and guarded recipe overrides populate the static JSON; the table
and details use the shared taxonomy labels. Neighbor retrieval is lazy; nearest
centroids, fitted kernels/GPs and trees are eager. Generic wrappers and Cubist with
optional neighbor correction require configuration-specific descriptions. Differing
recipe strategies show `Varies by recipe` without pooling capabilities.

## Estimator commitment

Commit applies the selected method's ranked summary recipe, or its saved recipe identity when restoring that same method. Construction requires selectable catalogue evidence and a supported preparation adapter. Errors retain the previous commitment. The exported proxy preserves frame, clean_frame, roles and preprocessing and replaces its terminal data_models step. A Learning processing record names the committed model and recipe. No fit occurs. A change to upstream proxy identity invalidates this session commitment. The footer distinguishes the committed estimator from a different pending row choice. Predictors are selected before model fitting, preventing target leakage.

The card-owned JSON `model_choice` field records `selected_method`, `selected_recipe`, and `committed_recipe` as stable catalogue identities. Table rebuilds restore a saved row after the browser's view binding is ready, without subscribing selection writes to user clicks; subsequent user selection remains authoritative. Sorting does not change identities. The committed recipe is rebuilt separately on restoration and validated against current outcome, requirements, runtime and construction support. Unavailable saved commitments produce a footer explanation without substitution. Configurations without this field retain the uncommitted default. Browser tests round-trip an actual downloaded configuration into a fresh app, with a selected row different from the committed recipe, and verify that subsequent changes can be committed.


Implicit resampling means internal validation/tuning splits, excluding bootstrap training and subsampling. The versioned-recipe registry `implicit_resampling.json` records reviewed construction parameters, package versions, statuses and reasons. Parameter/version drift and unlisted recipes produce Unreviewed, never an inferred No. `assess_profiles` adds this evidence without importing model libraries or changing capability/probe evidence. `_analyze` resolves automatic histogram early stopping conservatively from current cleaned-row counts, then adds a separate resampling exclusion: an existing upstream EvaluationPlan (including an invalid/stale plan) permits only No; no plan permits only Yes. Conditional/Unreviewed recipes are excluded in both cases. Presence is distinct from plan readiness.

The table includes Implicit resampling (Yes/No/Conditional/Unreviewed), preserving all statuses when grouping visible recipes. ShowAll reveals excluded rows without making them selectable. Reasons appear in readiness and recipe details. `model_commit.commit_problem` blocks excluded rows with the resampling reason, covering direct commit and restored committed recipes. No estimator is silently substituted or reconfigured, and no fit is performed to determine this indicator.


`Pred throughput` displays Low/Medium/High documentation-informed model-only guidance from `prediction_throughput.json`. Each predictive recipe has a rating, interpretation, evidence category, sources, exact construction and reviewed package version; registry-level policy defines direction and assumptions. High means greater expected throughput. These are qualitative expert judgments of documented inference mechanisms, not measured rates or documentation-prescribed labels. Unknown or configuration/version-drifted recipes show Unreviewed. The method table takes the rating from its ranked representative recipe, preserving the existing per-recipe filtering contract; no pooling or best-case rating across recipes. Reasons and evidence remain in JSON, not additional table columns. Capability/probe evidence, eligibility and commits are unchanged.


CatBoost's `catboost_strings` construction is supported through lazy-imported, top-level PreparedCatBoostRegressor/Classifier subclasses. They retain the native constructor, parameter paths, tags and cloning/pickling behavior. prepare_predictors preserves numeric NaNs and converts categorical/object/string/bool columns with typed nonmissing tokens and a disjoint missing marker. At fit, categorical names are inferred from the actual prepared DataFrame, so selected-away categorical columns do not leave stale cat_features indices. Native fit kwargs (including sample_weight) are forwarded. Numerical-only input uses an empty categorical list. Configuration still records the original catalogue recipe identity; committing/restoring creates an unfitted adapter. External package fingerprints include estimator base classes so local adapters retain their CatBoost version dependency. Regression covers a numeric-only saved Gaussian Process choice replaced by CatBoost, exported estimator identity and saved commitment, plus mixed-input regression/classification and spawned fold evaluation.


#### Multiple candidate methods

Select one or more method rows (Ctrl/Command-click adds rows) and press **Commit**.
All selected methods are validated before the candidate set is committed; an
invalid recipe leaves the previous commitment intact. One applicable recipe is
retained per selected method. Details describe the first selected method.

Proxy-data stores stable recipe IDs, method names and independent unfitted model
pipelines, including each method's preparation. These are alternative endings,
not an ensemble. Shared upstream transformations stay outside the alternatives.
With one candidate, ordinary training behaves as before. With several candidates,
a consumer must choose a candidate explicitly or use Pipeline tuning; the first
candidate is never silently used for training. Configuration JSON preserves both
the selected method list and the committed recipe list. Legacy single-method
configuration fields remain readable. Changing upstream data requires recommitment.

Candidate objects are stored in proxy_data._model_candidates and exposed through
model_candidates as cloned estimators. with_model_candidates validates the complete
set before returning a successor, preserving data, evaluation metadata and shared
preprocessing. pipeline_for_training(candidate_id) resolves a branch explicitly;
without an ID an unresolved multi-candidate set raises. The accepted final pipeline
stores its selected candidate ID and retains the original alternatives. Candidate
identity/settings participate in equality and tuning identity; no fitted state is
published. Committed UI state is a source/candidate-list tuple. selected_methods and
committed_recipes coexist with compatibility singleton fields in bookmark output.
